title: Inside the Underground Market for Know Your Client Services
description: Cybercriminals operate an underground market offering forged identity documents, deepfake videos, and live verification services to bypass Know Your Client (KYC) checks used by financial institutions. These services include generating fake passports, driver’s licenses, social security cards, and manipulated biometric verification to create fraudulent verified accounts. The market also provides ongoing support to maintain access to these accounts. Financial institutions are advised to use combined detection methods, including document and facial image integrity checks, unpredictable live verification prompts, and device fingerprinting to detect such fraud.
aiSummary: The underground market for KYC services involves the sale of forged identity documents, AI-generated or manipulated biometric media, and human-assisted live verification to circumvent identity verification processes at banks and cryptocurrency exchanges. Operators tailor identity packages with consistent personal details and supporting documents to pass automated and manual KYC checks. Techniques include deepfake videos that mimic live verification prompts and human operators completing live checks using prepared identity materials. Sellers also offer post-verification support to help buyers maintain control over fraudulent accounts. Monitoring of criminal forums reveals extensive advertising and recruitment for these services, highlighting a sophisticated ecosystem enabling identity fraud and money laundering.
aiImpact: This activity enables cybercriminals to conceal their true identities, bypass KYC controls, open fraudulent accounts, and launder money through financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms. It undermines the integrity of customer due diligence processes, increasing the risk of financial fraud and regulatory non-compliance for affected organizations. The persistence of these services and ongoing support after account creation complicate detection and remediation efforts.
